A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SciEvents and EXCEEDS, retaining the same underlying corpus and task schema despite substantial revisions. Text, equations, tables, figures and all appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original SciEvents dataset statistics, extraction experiments, complex-scenario evaluations and model ablations in Tables 1–5.

after.justification: V2 reports original extraction experiments and ablations, supplemented by error analyses, runtime measurements and detailed dataset analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Sections 5.2–5.3 replace v1's CLN-generated grid and combined Biaffine/BiAttention predictions with token normalization, pair representations incorporating distance embeddings, and residual convolutional grid refinement. Cross-entropy/softmax prediction becomes multi-label categorical cross-entropy with zero-threshold decisions. These change the architecture, objective and inference procedure while retaining the HTL/THL/EAL concept.

E1.justification: Extraction training and evaluation remain on SciEvents' 2,508 ACL 2019–2022 abstracts, with the same event schema and discontinuous, overlapping, reverse-order and sub-event scenarios. V2 broadens descriptive comparisons with other corpora, but adds no extraction benchmark. The DICE/Maccrobat-EE statistical comparison is retained under a different name.

E2.justification: The main comparison retains OneIE, PAIE and BartGen, removes UIE, and adds ScentedEAE, EEQA, Tagprime, DEEIA, DEGREE and KnowCoder. The complex-scenario comparison also expands substantially, including BartGen, which appeared only in v1's main comparison.

E3.justification: EXCEEDS changes from BERT, batch size 1 and 30 epochs to RoBERTa-large, batch size 2 and 20 epochs. Tagprime replaces the word-word relation model supplying triggers to retained argument-only baselines. The split ratio and five core metrics remain, but Table 4 stops reporting trigger classification for discontinuous and reverse-order subsets.

E4.justification: Biaffine/BiAttention ablations are replaced by Contextual/Grid Refiner ablations, also evaluated on complex subsets. V2 adds identification-error and type-confusion analyses in Figures 4–5, computational-cost measurements, and detailed analyses of document length and complex-structure distributions in Appendix H.

E5.justification: V1 reports averages from at least three experiments without dispersion estimates. V2 specifies three independent runs and introduces systematic ± uncertainty reporting across overall, complex-scenario and ablation results. The meaning of ± is not defined, and neither an increase in runs nor significance testing is documented.

E6.justification: Result sets are extensively replaced and expanded. Table 3 reports EXCEEDS AC/EC F1 of 41.85/47.60 in v1 and 43.20/48.25 for the revised setup in v2; these are not controlled performance gains. OneIE now leads TI. V2 also adds numerous baseline, error-analysis, runtime and dataset-statistics results.

T1.justification: Appendix D newly derives componentwise computational and memory scaling, including O(l²Cg + l²|R|) grid storage. Appendix A discusses potentially exponentially many candidate decoding paths. V1 contains neither analysis; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central SciEvents-plus-EXCEEDS contributions remain. V2 removes the assertion that SciEvents is the first scientific event-extraction dataset and replaces the introduction's superiority-on-all-tasks claim with consistently strong performance. Event correlation remains part of the work but is no longer a separately enumerated contribution.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive limitations concerning abstract-only data, missing multimodal/full-text information and restricted ACL/NLP coverage. Its new error interpretation identifies missed nuggets and semantically similar labels as major bottlenecks, extending v1's discussion of complex-form rarity and the original model components.

D1.justification: V2 adds decoding pseudocode, grid/warm-up/dropout hyperparameters, GPU specifications, runtime information, TextEE and baseline-adaptation details, and much richer annotation guidance. It supplies a concrete repository address where v1 only mentions GitHub. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation, although v1's explicit AdamW optimizer specification is omitted.

R1.justification: V2 develops a more specific comparison with approaches including RexUIE, Mirror and KnowCoder, positioning EXCEEDS around raw-text input and an EE-only, single-dataset setting. Citations are substantially revised for newer methods and resources, while v1's explicit connection to Li et al.'s word-word NER approach is removed.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work and dataset narrative are extensively rewritten, with clearer organization around density and complexity. Annotation procedures, remuneration and distributions are reorganized into appendices, and schema explanations are expanded. The title, acronym expansion and complex-nugget terminology also change.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the motivating example and architecture, adds a grid illustration and error plots, and removes v1's dataset-construction diagram. The main results table becomes an F1 summary with ablation rows, while precision/recall results move to appendix tables. Distribution displays are redesigned and expanded, and annotation screenshots are added.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation and reproducibility through broader baseline comparisons, uncertainty reporting, diagnostic analyses, and detailed decoding, implementation and annotation documentation. Explicit applicability limits and narrower superiority claims improve calibration. Undefined ± statistics and a remaining mismatch between the claimed uniform grid-refiner benefit and Table 3's TI result limit these gains, but the overall improvement in evidence and assessability is substantial. Changed settings prevent treating higher scores as controlled architectural gains.
